officials.name: Anne Dunn
officials.bio: Anne Dunn has served on the Brentwood City Commission since 1990, becoming the first woman elected Mayor in 1997 and re-elected in 2003. She currently serves on the Brentwood Historic Commission and previously served on the Planning Commission and International Board. Born in Belfast, Ireland, Anne was raised in North Carolina and is a former teacher and Allstate underwriter.

officials.name: Janet Donahue
officials.bio: Janet Donahue was elected to the City Commission in May 2025. She is an Emergency Medicine Physician and has served on the Brentwood Planning Commission since 2014, becoming chair in 2016. She is married to Sean Donahue and has four children.

officials.name: Ken Travis
officials.bio: Ken Travis was first elected to the City Commission in 2015 and is serving his third term, having also served on the Planning Commission and as Vice Mayor. He is retired from GE Healthcare after 39 years of service and holds a Marketing degree from Memphis State University. Ken, who relocated to Brentwood in 2001 with his wife Rhonda, is an active member of Holy Family Catholic Church and has two daughters and two grandchildren.

officials.name: Kim Smithson Gawrys
officials.bio: Kim Smithson Gawrys and her husband, Steve, are retired small business owners. She was a certified State of Tennessee Life & Health Insurance Instructor.

officials.name: Stevan Pippin
officials.bio: On July 14, Stevan Pippin was appointed as the seventh member of the Brentwood City Commission. Pippin is the owner and CEO of Stevan Pippin Productions and House of Pip Music. Stevan is married to Leslie Pippin, and the couple's daughter, Lindsay Pippin Baleka, lives in Spring Hill, Tennessee.

officials.name: Nelson Andrews
officials.bio: Nelson Andrews was elected in 2019 and is serving his second term as a City Commissioner. He is the President of Andrews Transportation Group and holds degrees from Vanderbilt University. He is married to Trish Andrews, has four children, and has lived in Brentwood since 1979.

officials.name: Rhea E. Little, III
officials.bio: Rhea E. Little, III was first elected to the City Commission in 2009 and recently served as Mayor. He owns Rhea Little Tire & Auto Repair, a fourth-generation family business in Brentwood, and has served on the Rotary Club of Brentwood Board of Directors.

officials.name: Bill Estes
officials.bio: Dr. Bill Estes was first elected to the City Council in 2006. He came to Cleveland in 1998 as an Assistant Professor of Education at Lee University and serves on the Cleveland Municipal Planning Commission and the Greenway Board. Prior to his council service, he was a public schoolteacher, assistant principal, and principal.

officials.name: Dan Moore
officials.bio: Dan Moore was appointed to the City Council on September 1st, 2024.

officials.name: David May
officials.bio: Councilman May has a long history of service to Cleveland, starting as a fire department volunteer and later serving as CFD chief for 14 years. He was a founding member of the 911 board and has volunteered on numerous projects and committees. A state-licensed contractor, he is married to Linda May and has two children.

officials.name: Duane Goff
officials.bio: Duane Goff was elected District 5 Councilman on September 1, 2024. A Cleveland native and Lee University graduate, he has been a local business owner for over two decades and is actively involved in community service, including roles with Bradley County Fire and Rescue and the Cleveland Entrepreneurial Task Force.

officials.name: Ken Webb
officials.bio: Ken Webb joined the Cleveland City Council on August 2, 2018 as an At-Large member. Prior to his retirement in late 2016, he was President- CEO of Cleveland Utilities. His tenure at Cleveland Utilities covered twenty-nine years, twenty-six of which he was CFO and three as CEO.

officials.name: Marsha McKenzie
officials.bio: Marsha McKenzie was appointed to the City Council on February 10, 2021, and has been a Cleveland resident for 58 years. She has a background in business, owning and operating a furniture warehouse and home renovation business for many years. McKenzie also served as an associate Missionary overseas for five years, working with children's orphanages and street ministries.

officials.name: Tom Cassada
officials.bio: Tom Cassada graduated from Bradley County High School in 1981 and received his Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from Lee University in 1992. He is currently VP of Operations for ABCOR Packaging, a company he co-founded. Cassada was elected to the Cleveland City Council representing District 3 and sworn in on September 12, 2016.

officials.name: Allen Foster
officials.bio: It is truly an honor to serve as the Cumberland County Mayor. Allen Foster started his work as a public servant in 2002 on the Board of Education, then served on the County Commission from 2010-2018, and was elected County Mayor in 2018. He believes leadership is a job of service to those that elect the leaders.

officials.bio: Freddie O'Connell is the tenth mayor of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County. He served on the Metro Council from 2015 to 2023 representing District 19, which includes the downtown core, Germantown, and parts of North Nashville.

officials.name: SHAWN FENNELL
officials.bio: Shawn Fennell is not new to public service, having previously served as a county commissioner and on various boards and committees. These roles included chairman of the Sumner County Law Enforcement Committee and vice chairman of the Sumner County Planning Commission. He also served three elected terms with the Sumner County Sheriff’s Civil Service.

officials.name: STEVEN FANN
officials.bio: As a resident of Sumner County for more than 40 years, Steve Fann has a diverse business background including retail/convenience store owner, pallet manufacturing, and residential/commercial rental property. He has been involved in local youth and adult sports for 18 years. His goal is to help shape Gallatin to balance growth with preserving its history and small-city appeal, supporting law enforcement, and maintaining affordable property taxes.

officials.name: PASCAL JOUVENCE
officials.bio: Councilman Pascal Jouvence was elected to the District 3 seat in January 2023.

officials.name: TODD ALEXANDER
officials.bio: Todd Alexander was born and raised in rural Indiana and served 12 years in the U.S. Marine Corps before entering the ministry. He moved to Gallatin in 2013 and was sworn in as District 2 Councilman in January 2025, aiming to listen to residents' concerns, control growth, improve infrastructure, and support local businesses.

officials.name: PAIGE BROWN
officials.bio: Paige Brown is currently serving her third term as Mayor of Gallatin, Tennessee (named “Nicest Place in America” in 2017 by Readers’ Digest). Elected in November 2014, she previously served as Executive Director of the Gallatin Area Chamber of Commerce (2006-2014). A graduate of Florida State University, she worked as a news reporter and anchor in Florida.

officials.bio: The County Mayor is elected to a four year term by the citizens of Hamilton County to head the executive branch of Hamilton County Government. As the Chief Fiscal Officer for the County, it is the Mayor’s responsibility to oversee the preparation and administration of official budgets and financial reports. In conjunction with division heads, the Mayor manages the daily operations of County General Government and ensures that all applicable laws, policies, and resolutions are implemented.

officials.name: Austin Maxwell
officials.bio: Austin Maxwell, a native of Knoxville, TN, graduated from the University of Tennessee at Knoxville in 1988 and later received his MBA from MTSU in 2007. He retired as a Lieutenant Colonel from the Tennessee Army National Guard in 2017 after 20+ years of service, including deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq. Maxwell was elected to the Murfreesboro City Council in August 2022, with his current term expiring in 2030.

officials.name: Jami Averwater
officials.bio: As a Rutherford County native, Averwater has seen firsthand the growth of Murfreesboro and feels passionately about the City’s success. Averwater has served on the Murfreesboro Planning Commission since 2021 and recognizes it was this opportunity that led her to run for City Council. Jami Averwater’s first term began in 2022. Her current term expires in 2030.

officials.name: Kirt Wade
officials.bio: Kirt Wade was first elected to the Murfreesboro City Council in 2016. Wade’s current term expires in 2028. Wade earned his bachelor’s degree from California Southern University in Irving, California in 1995 after attending Jackson State Community College in Tennessee.

officials.name: Madelyn Scales Harris
officials.bio: Madelyn Scales Harris was first elected to the Murfreesboro City Council in 2010, with her current term expiring in 2030. A Murfreesboro native, she is a graduate of Middle Tennessee State University and retired from State Farm Insurance. Scales Harris comes from a family of "firsts," having been selected as the 1st Female Vice-Mayor, following her father, the 1st Black Male Vice-Mayor, and her mother, the 1st Black Female to serve on the Murfreesboro City Council.

officials.name: Shawn Wright
officials.bio: Shawn Wright was elected to the Murfreesboro City Council in 2020, with his current term expiring in 2028. A lifelong resident of Rutherford County, he holds a BBA from Middle Tennessee State University and an MBA from the University of Memphis. Wright is also a Realtor/real estate broker with CENTURY 21 Wright Realty.

officials.name: Shane McFarland
officials.bio: Shane McFarland was elected to the Murfreesboro City Council in 2006. McFarland was elected Mayor of Murfreesboro in 2014 and was elected as the youngest Mayor in the history of Murfreesboro. He has helped guide the 13th fastest growing City in the country with programs for renewed downtown development, recruiting corporate jobs, enhanced parks and recreation offerings, additional public safety facilities and a renewed focus on Customer Service.

officials.name: Bill Shacklett
officials.bio: Bill Shacklett was first elected to the Murfreesboro City Council in 2002 and served until 2006. He was re-elected in 2014 and his current term expires in 2028. A Murfreesboro native, he holds a Bachelor of Science from Middle Tennessee State University and runs Shacklett's Photography.

officials.name: Rogers Anderson
officials.address: 1320 W Main Street Suite 125 Franklin, TN 37064
officials.bio: The Tennessee Constitution provides for the election of an executive officer, which is referred to as the County Mayor, in each county. The County Mayor is elected by popular vote at the regular August election every four years, coinciding with the Governor's election, and may serve an unlimited number of terms. The County Mayor, formerly County Executive, is Chief Executive Officer of the county. The County Mayor exercises a role of leadership in county government and is responsible for the county's fiscal management and other executive functions.
